ideas.name: CATCHFlow — CATCH Preflight & Certificate Lineage
ideas.oneSentenceConcept: Pre-submission preflight and certificate lineage reconciliation for EU seafood importers using the mandatory CATCH system, preventing clearance failures before containers arrive at port.
ideas.elevatorPitch: For EU seafood importers, customs brokers, and freight forwarders, CATCHFlow provides a software-assisted preflight service that reconciles catch certificates, vessel identity, quantity allocations, processing statements, and representative delegations against CATCH's actual validation rules before submission — catching the cross-system failures that currently strand containers at EU ports.
ideas.detailedDescription: CATCH became mandatory for EU seafood imports on 10 January 2026. By August 2026, the EU Market Advisory Council publicly called for operational stabilisation, citing recurring technical failures, clearance delays, and divergent Member State implementation. The durable problem is cross-system certificate lineage: vessel → catch → catch certificate → exporter → processor → processing statement → shipment → importer → CATCH → customs. CATCHFlow preflights every step before commitment.

atAGlance.urgency: live — system mandatory since Jan 2026, operational pain documented Aug 2026
atAGlance.primaryBuyer: EU seafood importers, customs brokers, freight forwarders handling covered fishery products
atAGlance.firstArtifact: Software-assisted preflight report for one real CATCH shipment: certificate lineage, quantity allocation, delegation check
atAGlance.paymentGate: €99–€299 per shipment preflight or small monthly bundle; offer manually before building software
atAGlance.primaryRisk: Commission improves CATCH bulk upload, delegation, and validation within 90 days eliminating short-term pain
atAGlance.killCondition: Zero payment interest from 50 importer/broker contacts; or quantity reconciliation shown to already be handled by existing import-management tools

ideas.productConcept: Pre-submission preflight of CATCH import documentation: reconcile catch certificate lineage, vessel identity, species codes, quantity allocations across certificates, processing statements, importer identity, representative delegation, and Member State destination routing — then report pass/fail with specific fixable failures before the importer commits the shipment.
ideas.mvpApproach: Software-assisted service: accept paperwork for one upcoming shipment, run preflight manually, deliver structured evidence report. Automate only the repeated failure modes discovered in first 20 cases.
ideas.landAndExpand: catch-certificate preflight → processing statements → quantity lineage → delegation/broker workflow → third-country integrations → full seafood-import regulatory evidence graph → TRACES-adjacent import systems → regulated food-import infrastructure
sources: EU TRACES / CATCH mandatory obligation: 10 January 2026
EU Market Advisory Council operational stabilisation call: 4 August 2026
CLECAT implementation complaints: early 2026
Financial Times port disruption reporting: early 2026
UK Fish Export Service / CATCH cross-system integration guidance: August 2026

ideas.name: CertFlow / HandshakeLab — CERTEX Regulatory Handshake Lab
ideas.oneSentenceConcept: A multi-formality regulatory handshake engine that simulates EU CSW-CERTEX clearance checks — quota consumption, authorization validation, certificate status — before customs declarations are submitted, starting with F-gas as the first vertical.
ideas.elevatorPitch: For customs brokers, importers, and customs software vendors, CertFlow predicts which customs declarations will fail CERTEX regulatory handshakes — quota reservations, authorization checks, certificate validity, schema transformation — before they enter the production submission queue.
ideas.detailedDescription: EU CSW-CERTEX connects national customs systems to non-customs EU regulatory systems, performing data transformation, quota consumption, authorization checks, and quantity management at clearance time. A shipment can appear fully correct inside an ERP while being machine-invalid at the CERTEX handshake. CertFlow builds the pre-declaration simulation layer: one formality pack at a time, starting with F-gas.

atAGlance.urgency: live — CERTEX operational; F-gas enforcement documented
atAGlance.primaryBuyer: Customs software vendors (SDK), customs brokers, industrial importers with CERTEX-covered formalities
atAGlance.firstArtifact: F-gas preflight: ERP import object → customs object → F-gas portal state → CERTEX checks
atAGlance.paymentGate: SDK licensing to customs software vendors; or per-declaration preflight fee
atAGlance.primaryRisk: CERTEX interface access remains government-only; customs software vendors bundle this before startup ships
atAGlance.killCondition: Cannot obtain test environment/interface access at reasonable cost; or F-gas pilot finds zero interest from customs brokers

ideas.productConcept: Multi-formality pre-declaration simulation engine. Adapters: CustomsDeclarationAdapter, FormalityAdapter, IdentityAdapter, QuantityLedger, StateMachine, RuleVersion, PreflightResult. First implementation: F-gas. Moat: production failure corpus built from real submission outcomes.
ideas.moat: Cross-vendor, cross-formality, cross-country, continuously updated, independent production failure knowledge accumulated from real submission cycles.
ideas.landAndExpand: F-gas preflight → second CERTEX formality → third → customs software SDK → cross-formality clearance prediction across 14+ formality types
sources: EU CSW-CERTEX Commission architecture documentation
CERTEX data transformation, quota-consumption, authorization check descriptions
CERTEX quantity management: reservation, consumption, release on customs outcome
F-gas as significant CERTEX customs-enforcement domain (Commission)

ideas.name: F-Gas Shipment & Quota Integrity Gate
ideas.oneSentenceConcept: Pre-declaration cross-system reconciliation gate for F-gas equipment imports, checking ERP product data against F-gas Portal registration, authorization remaining, and customs declaration fields before submission.
ideas.elevatorPitch: For refrigeration equipment importers and customs brokers, F-Gas Gate reconciles product F-gas content, importer registration, authorization remaining, and customs declaration fields in a single pre-declaration check — preventing clearance failures caused by quota exhaustion or declaration mismatches.
ideas.detailedDescription: EU F-gas regulation creates a heavily structured numeric compliance environment: registered importers, quota authorizations, HFC quota reference values fixed through 2029, GWP-weighted quantity calculations, CERTEX quota consumption at customs. The gate reconciles ERP product data + F-gas Portal state + customs declaration fields before submission.

atAGlance.urgency: live — F-gas regulation operational; quota reference values fixed 2027-2029
atAGlance.primaryBuyer: Refrigeration equipment importers, HVAC manufacturers, F-gas quota holders, customs brokers handling F-gas shipments
atAGlance.firstArtifact: Single-page pre-declaration reconciliation: product GWP, registration, authorization remaining, declaration fields
atAGlance.paymentGate: €99–€299 per preflight or monthly subscription for recurring importers
atAGlance.primaryRisk: Existing F-gas quota brokers already provide pre-declaration reconciliation; customs software vendors bundle F-gas checks
atAGlance.killCondition: Quota specialists confirm existing tools catch quota mismatches before declaration

ideas.productConcept: Cross-system pre-declaration gate: ERP product (model, gas type, GWP, net quantity) + F-gas Portal state (registration, authorization remaining) + customs declaration (CN/TARIC, procedure, supporting-document refs) → unified preflight result with quota shortfall calculation, registration status, and declaration field validation.
ideas.roleInPortfolio: Best first vertical for CertFlow (idea-416). If architecture generalizes, F-gas becomes Pack 1.
sources: EU F-gas Portal: registration, licensing, HFC quota workflows
Commission implementing decision: HFC quota reference values 2027-2029, June 2026
CERTEX documentation: quota-consumption checks, F-gas as significant enforcement domain

ideas.name: EPREL Retail-State Drift Monitor
ideas.oneSentenceConcept: Catalogue-scale monitor that maps a retailer's full SKU/GTIN catalogue to EPREL energy-label records and flags mismatched labels, wrong energy classes, stale PIS files, and cross-marketplace drift before enforcement actions.
ideas.elevatorPitch: For online retailers and marketplace operators selling energy-labelled products, EPREL Watch crawls the entire product catalogue, maps every SKU/GTIN to its EPREL registration, and identifies mismatches, stale Product Information Sheets, wrong energy classes, and cross-marketplace inconsistencies — at scale, automatically.
ideas.detailedDescription: EPREL is the EU authoritative registry for energy-labelled products. As of July 2026, EPREL supports GTIN-level identification and model pictures, enabling automated catalogue-level reconciliation. The drift monitor maps manufacturer→EPREL→PIM→retailer→marketplace and detects state divergence at each hop.

atAGlance.urgency: live — EPREL APIs public, GTIN support added July 2026
atAGlance.primaryBuyer: Large online retailers, marketplace operators, energy product category managers
atAGlance.firstArtifact: Free drift report for one mid-size retailer's full product range
atAGlance.paymentGate: Monthly monitoring subscription per catalogue size
atAGlance.primaryRisk: Retail/PIM vendors add EPREL synchronization as standard feature
atAGlance.killCondition: Enforcement risk minimal; or retail/PIM vendors bundle EPREL sync in next product cycle

ideas.productConcept: Catalogue crawler: ingest retailer SKU list → map GTIN/model to EPREL → check correct label, class, range, PIS, model identity, supplier state, QR relationship → report drift count by type and marketplace.
sources: EPREL public API and supplier documentation
Commission: GTIN and model pictures available from July 20 2026
EU Energy Labelling Regulation dealer obligations

ideas.name: Battery Health Attestation
ideas.oneSentenceConcept: Structured evidence layer that records the measurement method, software version, calibration, and data provenance behind every battery state-of-health value in an EU battery passport — enabling buyers to distinguish actual degradation from algorithm or calibration changes.
ideas.elevatorPitch: For second-life battery traders and EV fleet operators, Battery Health Attestation provides structured provenance behind every SOH value in a battery passport — so when a health reading changes, buyers can determine whether the battery degraded or whether the measurement method changed.
ideas.detailedDescription: A 2026 cross-manufacturer study of 1000+ EVs found significant variation between actual capacity degradation and BMS-reported SOH values. The EU Battery Regulation mandates SOH in battery passports but does not mandate measurement-method provenance. This is an evidence-quality problem creating distrust in second-life battery transactions.

atAGlance.urgency: developing — battery passport mandates active; second-life market growing
atAGlance.primaryBuyer: Second-life battery traders, battery recyclers, EV fleet operators, battery-passport platform vendors
atAGlance.firstArtifact: SOH attestation schema + one pilot battery record with full measurement provenance
atAGlance.paymentGate: API licensing to battery-passport platforms; or per-transaction attestation fee for second-life trades
atAGlance.primaryRisk: Battery diagnostics platforms add passport-linked provenance records
atAGlance.killCondition: Battery diagnostics incumbents confirmed to already handle measurement-method provenance
atAGlance.bestRole: Module within ProofOps / EvidenceGraph platform — not first standalone company

ideas.productConcept: SOH attestation record: battery_id, passport_version, soh_value, measurement_method, software_version, calibration_version, raw_input_provenance, bms_data_reference, independent_diagnostic_data, confidence, timestamp, signer.
sources: 2026 cross-manufacturer EV battery SOH variation study: 1000+ vehicles (arXiv)
EU Battery Regulation: SOH in battery passport mandate
BatteryPass-Ready: conformance/interoperability test environment development

ideas.name: Recall Propagation Proof
ideas.oneSentenceConcept: Evidence graph proving that a product recall propagated completely through an organisation — from Safety Gate notice to web listings disabled, WMS quarantined, fulfilment blocked, customer cohort resolved, and destruction documented.
ideas.elevatorPitch: For large multi-channel retailers facing GPSR enforcement, Recall Propagation Proof creates a timestamped evidence chain showing that a recall notice propagated through every affected system — catalogue, WMS, marketplace listings, fulfilment, customer communications — before the regulator asks.
ideas.detailedDescription: Generic Safety Gate monitoring is commoditised (SafeCart and scrapers). The gap is proving complete operational propagation: recall notice → affected GTINs/batch codes → web listings disabled → marketplace listings disabled → WMS inventory quarantined → fulfilment blocked → customer cohort resolved → communication sent → return/destruction evidence. This is an evidence problem, not a monitoring problem.

atAGlance.urgency: watch — GPSR enforcement increasing but pace uncertain
atAGlance.primaryBuyer: Large multi-channel retailers, marketplace operators, product safety/legal teams
atAGlance.firstArtifact: Recall propagation evidence report for one past recall event (retrospective audit)
atAGlance.paymentGate: Add-on module to WMS / OMS / marketplace management tools
atAGlance.primaryRisk: Existing product-safety platforms already cover cross-channel propagation evidence; GPSR enforcement minimal
atAGlance.killCondition: Existing product-safety platforms confirmed to cover multi-channel propagation evidence
atAGlance.bestRole: Module within Compliance OS or product-safety platform — not standalone priority

ideas.productConcept: Recall response evidence graph: recall_notice → affected_GTINs/batch_codes → web_listings_disabled → marketplace_listings_disabled → WMS_inventory_quarantined → fulfillment_blocked → customer_cohort_resolved → communication_sent → return/destruction_evidence. Timestamped, auditable, regulator-presentable.
ideas.promotionConditions: Promote to priority if: interviews show existing tools do NOT cover cross-channel propagation evidence; a retailer co-funds pilot after enforcement action; or GPSR enforcement demonstrably increases.
sources: Safety Gate (EU Product Safety Database) public API
SafeCart marketplace-scale recall matching (competitor)
EU General Product Safety Regulation (GPSR) enforcement obligations
